mascotLines: Clients can tap their card at the front desk now. I'll keep tapping my bowl.
Desktop sends one email for a whole batch of documents now. I also only need to hear "walk" once.
Jobs and Tasks remember your filters now. I remember every couch cushion I've ever hidden a treat under.
A new banner rounds up jobs stuck in the last stage. Herding is literally in my job description.

items.text: Take card payments in person on a card reader
items.desc: US firms using TaxDome Payments can now charge a client's card on a physical card reader at the front desk, right from TaxDome — the invoice is marked paid automatically and the client gets a receipt with their payment email. Readers can be ordered from Settings → Integrations → Payments; firms still on an older Stripe account type are asked to finish their account upgrade first.

items.text: Mark jobs stuck in the last stage complete in one click
items.desc: A new banner on the jobs list and pipeline page shows how many active jobs are sitting in the final stage and lets you mark them all complete at once, so finished work stops showing as "in progress" in your reports.

items.text: Jobs and Tasks remember your filters
items.desc: The filters you apply on the Jobs and Tasks lists are now kept when you leave the page or refresh, so you come back to the same view instead of setting them up again. Saved per browser, separate from presets.

items.text: Desktop app: one notification email per client, not one per document
items.desc: When you click Notify client on several documents for the same client within 30 seconds, the Desktop app now sends them together in one email. Before, the client got a separate email for every document.

items.text: Share button on Marketplace product pages
items.desc: Marketplace product pages now have a Share button that copies a link anyone at any firm can open — signed-in users land on that product in their own firm, and everyone else is asked to sign in first.

items.text: TRD AI no longer puts Form 8453 in Signature requests
items.desc: Form 8453 says right on it that the taxpayer shouldn't sign it, but Tax Return Delivery AI was placing it in Signature requests and most firms removed it by hand. It no longer lands there.

items.text: Click a service name to edit it
items.desc: In Billing → Services, the service name in the table is now clickable and opens the edit sidebar directly.

items.text: Billing Monitor dashboard
items.desc: The first of three ready-made dashboards in the new Reporting: one place to see what the firm invoiced, what it actually received and what clients still owe, with aged receivables and a comparison with the same period last year. Figures can be broken down by account, account tag and team member.

items.text: An optional AI plan with a free trial
items.desc: Firms would switch on a paid AI plan themselves, starting with a 14-day free trial, to keep using TaxDome's AI features such as Tax Return Delivery AI, AI renaming and the Atlas assistant.

items.text: New plan: bring the whole team, pay for the clients you serve
items.desc: A plan that includes your whole team and is priced by the clients you work with, instead of buying a licence for every person.

items.text: Buy client capacity up front at a lower rate
items.desc: Firms would be able to buy the client capacity they expect to need at purchase, at a better rate, instead of paying the top rate month by month as clients become active.

items.text: A meter for how many clients count toward your plan
items.desc: Shows how much of the firm's client allowance is already used and how fast it's filling, so the next bill isn't a surprise and extra capacity can be bought in time.

items.text: See exactly what you'll be charged before paying
items.desc: A clear breakdown of what's included and the total at checkout, so a firm's first bill matches what it agreed to.

items.text: Monthly extra-client charges on a predictable day
items.desc: Charges for clients above the plan's allowance would arrive on the same day each month with a clear explanation of what they're for.

items.text: Send client documents to Instead from TaxDome
items.desc: Firms that use Instead for tax planning would connect it in TaxDome and send a client's documents straight to it, instead of exporting and re-uploading them.

items.text: TRD: save your usual settings and apply them in one click
items.desc: Save a Tax Return Delivery's usual setup — reminders, approval, invoice statement, custom messages — once and reuse it, instead of toggling the same options for every return.

items.text: Checklists from your firm's own templates
items.desc: Firms would be able to save their own checklist templates with items already filled in and apply them to a client, instead of typing out the list item by item every time.

items.text: Checklists for a whole client book from a Drake backup
items.desc: Upload one Drake backup and get personalized document checklists generated for matched individual clients in one go, instead of building them client by client. Starting as a small limited launch.

items.text: TRD: signature fields placed for you
items.desc: Automatically placing signature, date and initial fields on a Tax Return Delivery's signature pages (like Form 8879), instead of dragging each one in by hand for every signer.

items.text: Heads-up on Stripe information requests before payouts pause
items.desc: Stripe sometimes asks newly connected firms for extra details after setup, and firms often miss the email until payouts are already on hold. This would move those requests into onboarding or show them right inside TaxDome, so payouts keep flowing.

items.text: Proposal expiration dates
items.desc: Set an expiration date on a proposal so it can no longer be signed after the deadline, instead of tracking stale proposals and deleting them by hand.

items.text: Desktop app: the new version as smooth as the old one
items.desc: Ongoing work to make sure firms moving to the new Desktop app can print, upload and use Drive just as reliably as before, so nobody feels the need to switch back to the old version.

items.text: Roll a checklist forward into the new season
items.desc: Carrying a client's prior-season checklist into the new season in one action instead of rebuilding it from zero every year.

items.text: More than one checklist per client
items.desc: Letting a firm keep several checklists per client at once — for example, one per tax type and period — instead of a new checklist overwriting the old one.

items.text: Fixed: clients couldn't sign documents sent for a qualified e-signature (QES)
items.desc: When a firm sent a signature request with the QES option on, it was created without any signature fields, so the client didn't see it as needing a signature and had no way to start signing. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: some clients couldn't finish self-signup
items.desc: If a client's answer on the firm's signup form started a pipeline whose first step automatically sends an invoice set to use client credit, the whole signup failed with an error and there was no workaround. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: Desktop: edits saved in Acrobat, Foxit or Excel on Drive didn't reach the web
items.desc: Some programs save by writing a temporary file and swapping it in. The Desktop app skipped that kind of save, so the web kept showing the old version (and with Excel the document could even disappear from the account). Fixed, so the saved version is uploaded.

items.text: Fixed: Desktop: a quick second save of a new Word or Excel file made a "(2)" copy
items.desc: Saving a brand-new Word or Excel file on TaxDome Drive and saving it again within a few seconds could create an extra "(2)" copy holding the latest changes — or lose the second save entirely. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: Desktop bulk delete could remove a file you'd unchecked
items.desc: If you unchecked a file using the keyboard while the "Delete N files?" confirmation was open, it was still deleted along with the others. Fixed, so only the files actually selected are deleted.

items.text: Fixed: Desktop: larger printed or uploaded files failing as "Unknown upload failure"
items.desc: On slower connections or VPNs, bigger files sent from the Desktop app could time out and fail with a vague "Unknown upload failure" and no retry. Temporary server errors are now retried, and when the server rejects a file (for example, a virus-scan hit) the app shows the real reason.

items.text: Fixed: Jobs page could turn into "page not found" after a bulk update
items.desc: After a bulk action on the jobs list or pipeline page — like bulk edit, status change or the new Mark complete banner — the whole page could sometimes be replaced by a "page not found" screen until you navigated away. Fixed.

items.text: Fixed: deleted documents stayed in Trash past 120 days
items.desc: Documents are supposed to be permanently removed from Trash 120 days after they're deleted, but older ones were staying there. Fixed, so firms relying on that cleanup for data retention get it.

items.text: Fixed: client app showed only 15 requests waiting for action
items.desc: In the client mobile app, the "Waiting for action" list and counter stopped at 15 requests, so clients with more couldn't reach the rest. Fixed — the counter shows the real total and every request can be opened.

poll.label: Card payments on a reader at the front desk

mystery: A TurboTax autosave quirk was quietly turning every autosave into a new 4 MB document on TaxDome Drive — about one every five minutes. One firm piled up roughly 3,000 of them in ten days before this week's Desktop update taught the app to ignore those backup files.
